ADLBHY contains one record per lab test code per sample, per subject for the Hy’s Law based analysis parameters.
ADLBHY is derived from the ADLBC (Laboratory Results Chemistry Analysis Data) analysis dataset.

A separate analysis dataset will be provided containing the lab parameters needed for the assessment of Hy’s Law. An abnormal flag will be assigned to indicate whether a subject meets the criteria for a modified Hy’s Law assessment of liver function, defined as: 1. Transaminase (SGPT/ALT or SGOT/AST) elevations (i.e., >1.5*ULN) and 2. Bilirubin elevated to greater than 1.5*ULN.

Shift tables summarizing whether or not a subject’s status changed from baseline during the treatment period will be provided for changes based on threshold ranges and changes based on Hy’s Law. In these tables a subject will be categorized as normal or abnormal (i.e., outside the threshold range) at baseline. During the treatment phase, the most extreme value will be used to categorize a patient as normal or abnormal during the treatment phase.

[1] A subject is counted only once for each analyte. A change will be considered shifting from normal at baseline to abnormal or from abnormal at baseline to normal at any visit during the treatment. The treatment period is defined as any planned visit after Week 0 (Visit 3), up to and including Week 24 (Visit 12).
Bilirubin 2 x ULN and Transaminase 1.5 x ULN

Native ItemDefs make SHIFT1 missing for ALT, AST and BILI. For BILIHY, TRANSHY and HYLAW they describe baseline/current category pairs for high-to-normal, normal-to-normal and normal-to-high. The data guide describes sample-level records. SAP page-17 and page-39 discuss treatment-summary tables, with one subject counted per analyte. Those statements are retained as context and are not imposed as a worst-on-treatment aggregation on this per-assessment variable.

The SAP separate modified-Hy assessment uses the narrative bilirubin threshold, whereas the treatment-table shell labels a different bilirubin threshold. In addition, the ratio of the value to its LLN (i.e., value/LLN) and to its ULN (i.e., value/ULN) will be calculated for inclusion in the datasets, but not analyzed. These ratios will allow a quick searching for subjects with values greater than 1.5*ULN, for example, without the use of additional flags.

A separate analysis dataset will be provided containing the lab parameters needed for the assessment of Hy’s Law. An abnormal flag will be assigned to indicate whether a subject meets the criteria for a modified Hy’s Law assessment of liver function, defined as: 1. Transaminase (SGPT/ALT or SGOT/AST) elevations (i.e., >1.5*ULN) and 2. Bilirubin elevated to greater than 1.5*ULN.

Laboratory values will be assigned a flag of abnormal (high or low) if the value is outside the threshold range (defined as significantly beyond the normal range, i.e., >1.5*ULN or <.5*LLN) or if the value is significantly different from the value observed at the preceding scheduled visit (i.e., absolute value of the change from previous value is larger than the 50% of the normal range, ULN-LLN).

interpretations: The exact-section adapter omits the retained native parameter-level ItemDef comments and their ValueListRef association. Original XML was inspected independently; its OIDs and line pointers are recorded in adlbhy3-notes.json. Native summaries are not presented as verified citations.

Native ordinary-parameter ItemDefs use the identifier R21AHI in the positive threshold condition and R2A1HI in the subsequent nonmissing condition. Independent schema inspection finds the latter source field, while the former identifier is not present. Native derived-parameter ItemDefs assign missing. The source spelling and conditional precedence require a reviewer decision; they are not silently normalized into a literal rule.

The own ordinary-row helper checks R2A1HI, assigns missing when that source is missing, then applies the high threshold and assigns Y or N. All three derived row families assign blank. The spelling-normalized diagnostic reproduces that conditional structure from published upstream REF.R2A1HI only.

The generic laboratory abnormality flag described on SAP page-12 includes low thresholds and change from the preceding visit. Its wording does not identify CRIT1FL and is not imported into this separate criterion evaluation. The separate modified-Hy assessment also includes a combined transaminase/bilirubin condition; it does not define this individual-test flag.
CRIT1FL__R2A1HI_DIAGNOSTIC is an unclaimed source-spelling reading. It does not claim the native literal with the unresolved identifier, and does not copy REF.CRIT1FL.
claims.assessment: The Y/N domain is citable. The actual native parameter-level conditions are omitted by the adapter and contain an unresolved source spelling.

_CRIT1FL:
        case:
          - when: "ADLBC.R2A1HI IS NULL"
            then: "''"
          - when: "ADLBC.R2A1HI > 1.5"
            then: "'Y'"
          - otherwise: "'N'"
      _CRIT1FN:
        case:
          - when: "ADLBC.R2A1HI IS NULL"
            then:
          - when: "ADLBC.R2A1HI > 1.5"
            then: 1.0
          - otherwise: 0.0

Whitespace padding is removed from the published upstream flag before applying the codelist crosswalk. Missing or non-enumerated flag text maps to missing; no category outside the two documented source codes is invented.

The own implementation computes the flag and its numeric representation from the same upstream ratio for ordinary rows and assigns both missing on every derived row family. The formal probe tests only the documented flag-to-code rule, not the correctness of that upstream ratio or flag.
